items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: They assembled a big band for Earl Fatha Hines, and we played at the Riverboat. And I did a week of that with him

ctx.x: When you, you kind of caught the tail end of the heyday of the big bands I guess, after they kind of had a tough time after World War II. Did you get to do much big band playing because of that?

I didn’t do too much big band, very little big band myself, except like I said if I played some local dances. But I did have a chance to play with one big band that I enjoyed. They assembled a big band for Earl Fatha Hines, and we played at the Riverboat. And I did a week of that with him and then I went on to do something else. But that was wonderful. Well I had been out with Earl for a while. We had dome some quartet things. Oliver Jackson, my wonderful friend Oliver who is gone now — I sure miss him also, he…
What kind of, have you done any non-jazz kind of work? Done any rhythm & blues, that type of thing?
